chapterNote: Three verses, and Spurgeon said it was one of the shortest psalms to read and one of the longest to learn. David — king, warrior, poet, the most accomplished man in Israel — describes a soul he has had to work on: no proud heart, no eyes lifted too high, no pacing around in matters too great and too wonderful for him. The picture he reaches for is the most domestic in the Psalter: a weaned child with its mother. Not a nursing infant, demanding and fretful, but a child past weaning, who has stopped wanting the breast and now leans against the mother simply because she is there. That is what he has done to his soul — leveled it, quieted it, weaned it from its demands without weaning it from its God. And the last line hands the lesson to the nation: Israel, hope in the LORD, from now on and for all time. Only a weaned soul can wait like that.

1.text: A song of ascents, of David. LORD, my heart is not proud, and my eyes are not raised too high; I do not busy myself with great matters or with things too wonderful for me.
1.amp: A Song [shir] of degrees [maaloth] of David. LORD [YHWH], my heart [leb] is not haughty [gabah — lifted high], nor mine eyes [ayin] lofty [rum]: neither do I exercise ['walk', halak, the KJV margin] myself in great matters [gadol], or in things too high ['wonderful', pala, the KJV margin] for me.
1.notes: Three denials from Israel's most accomplished man: no gabah (H1361) leb (H3820), no rum (H7311) enayim (H5869) — the proud heart and the lifted eyes — and no halak (H1980), no walking about, among gedolot (H1419) and niphlaot (H6381), the great and the too-wonderful. Not anti-intellectual; a refusal to pace the corridors above his pay grade (cf. Deuteronomy 29:29).

2.text: Surely I have settled and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother; my soul within me is like a weaned child.
2.amp: Surely I have behaved [shavah — leveled, composed] and quieted [damam — stilled] myself ['my soul', nephesh, the KJV margin], as a child that is weaned [gamal] of his mother [em]: my soul [nephesh] is even as a weaned child [gamal].
2.notes: shavah and damam (H7737, H1826): the nephesh (H5315) leveled like a field and hushed. The image is precise — gamul (H1580), a WEANED child, not a nursing one: a child who has stopped demanding the breast and rests against the em (H517) for her own sake. Contentment is a soul weaned from its wants without being weaned from its God.

3.text: Israel, hope in the LORD, from now on and for all time.
3.amp: Let Israel [Yisrael] hope [yachal — wait expectantly] in the LORD [YHWH] from henceforth ['from now', the KJV margin] and for [ad] ever [olam].
3.notes: The private stillness becomes national counsel: yachal (H3176), the waiting-hope, me-attah ve-ad-olam (H5704, H5769), 'from now and on to forever' — Psalm 113:2's formula. A weaned soul is the only kind that can hope patiently; Yisrael (H3478) is told to become what David has become.
